items.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I set up the music publishing. I set up all his things to do – so many different things. ... I think I was taking him too fast, too far for his way of thinking.

ctx.x: That became my measure for pretty much – I had to have that kind of an emotional feeling of what everybody that I had to work with was doing. I had to get an emotional contact with them. Some things weren’t that emotional, but the people were the kind of people that you could work with or that I felt that needed to be – needed to have some help in what they were trying to do. When they came to me, I accepted them, took them on, or they were recommended to me by somebody like Cannonball. Because Wes Montgomery…

items.title: John Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: Wes Montgomery tells a story about, I wasn’t with them and he went to Spain.

ctx.x: Somebody take the phone out of your hands—

Yeah. I needed somebody to take the phone, that’s right, that’s right. So it was building and all of a sudden I’m managing ten or twelve people, which is not, doesn’t make sense, because you can not do the job. I learned that quickly, you know, having that many people just wasn’t, didn’t make sense. I had a lot of help, I had different people working with me, but everybody depended on me for the decisions and they wanted to talk to me about anything. They wanted to talk to the Road Managers and everything. My son…
